title: Custom Zscaler connectors for Slack, Salesforce, Microsoft and Google tenants: credentials, scopes and permissions

prose.text: A custom connector is the client-side way to authorize a SaaS tenant with a minimum set of credentials. {{purpose}} How tenants are listed and reauthorized is in [[zia.casb.tenants]].

prose.label: Salesforce.
prose.text: {{salesforce-credentials}} {{salesforce-user}} {{salesforce-client-app}} {{salesforce-org-settings}} {{salesforce-key}} {{salesforce-authorize}} The tenants page limits trusted domains and users to email tenants {{divergence:trusted-profiles-scope}}, and the SSPM permissions page is in [[zia.sspm.permissions:salesforce-inevitable-write]]. {{salesforce-permissions}} {{salesforce-production-permissions}} The Modify All Data row for SSPM differs between the two pages {{divergence:salesforce-modify-all-data}}. What the production steps give and omit is open {{gap:salesforce-production-values}}.

prose.label: Microsoft.
prose.text: {{microsoft-apps-and-methods}} The private key requirement for MIP disagrees with the page's own table and steps {{divergence:microsoft-mip-client-secret}}. {{microsoft-registration}} {{microsoft-pem-files}} {{microsoft-consent-url}} {{microsoft-app-specifics}} Dynamics 365 has no permissions table {{gap:dynamics-permissions}}.

checks.do: Whether the application's connector uses the credential type the page requires, and for MIP use the divergence rather than either statement.
Whether a Salesforce SSPM question about Modify All Data rests on the divergence, not on one page's table.

purpose.statement: The service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to Salesforce, to Gmail, Google Cloud Platform, Google Drive and Google Workspace, and to specific Slack workspaces. For Salesforce, the Microsoft applications and those Google applications, the service can use a minimum set of credentials instead of full administrator credentials; for Slack it enables selective monitoring of specific workspaces within the Slack enterprise account for DLP and Malware scanning.

quotes: The Zscaler service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to Salesforce. With this functionality, instead of requiring full administrator credentials, the Zscaler service can use a minimum set of credentials to access Salesforce.
With this functionality, instead of requiring full administrator credentials, the Zscaler service can use a minimum set of credentials to access your Microsoft applications.
The Zscaler service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to Gmail, Google Cloud Platform, Google Drive, and Google Workspace.
With this functionality, instead of requiring full administrator credentials, the Zscaler service can use a minimum set of credentials to access these Google applications.

The Zscaler service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to specific Slack workspaces. With this functionality, you can enable selective monitoring of specific workspaces within your Slack enterprise account for DLP and Malware scanning.

slack-credentials.statement: A custom connector for Slack for DLP and Malware scanning needs the Slack workspace ID, client ID and client secret during tenant onboarding in the Admin Console, plus the right permissions; the Slack app's distribution is activated under Manage Distribution in Settings to allow installation.

quotes: When you create a custom connector for Slack for DLP and Malware scanning, you must provide the Slack workspace ID, client ID, client secret during tenant onboarding in the Zscaler Admin Console so that the Zscaler service can access the application.
You must also configure the right permissions so that Zscaler can securely authorize the application.
Go to Manage Distribution under Settings and click Activate Distribution to allow installation.

slack-scopes.statement: The Slack app's bot token scopes are channels:manage, channels:read, chat:write, groups:write, im:write, mpim:write, groups:read, im:read, files:write and mpim:read; its user token scopes are admin.teams:read, auditlogs:read, channels:read, discovery:read, discovery:write, files:read, im:read, files:write and team:read. The discovery:read and discovery:write scopes are request-only, with the page asking to share the App ID.

quotes: - channels:manage - channels:read - chat:write - groups:write - im:write - mpim:write - groups:read - im:read - files:write - mpim:read
- admin.teams:read - auditlogs:read - channels:read - discovery:read - discovery:write - files:read - im:read - files:write - team:read
The discovery:read and discovery:write scopes are request-only scopes.
Share your App ID.

slack-workspace-id.statement: The Slack workspace ID depends on the account type, Enterprise Grid or Non-Grid (Enterprise Select, Pro or Business+). For Enterprise Grid it is copied with Copy Workspace ID under All Workspaces; for Non-Grid it is the T-prefixed ID, the segment after /client/ in a URL such as https://app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXXX/CXXXXXXX.

quotes: This ID depends on your Slack account type, for example, Enterprise Grid or Non-Grid (Enterprise Select, Pro, or Business+).
Go to All Workspaces under Workspaces.
Select Copy Workspace ID.
The address bar shows the URL https://app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXXX/CXXXXXXX
Copy the T-prefixed ID from the URL (the segment after /client/).

salesforce-credentials.statement: A Salesforce custom connector for SSPM Scan needs the client ID, client secret, integration user's username and instance URL in the Admin Console; DLP and Malware scanning SaaS API onboarding additionally needs the Malware and DLP quarantine library names. The two libraries are named Zscaler_Quarantine (unique name Malware_Quarantine) and Zscaler_DLP_Quarantine (unique name DLP_Quarantine), with permission set to Library Administrator.

quotes: When you create a custom connector for Salesforce for SSPM Scan, you must provide the client ID, client secret, integration user's username, and instance URL in the Zscaler Admin Console so that the Zscaler service can access the application.
For Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Malware scanning SaaS API onboarding, you additionally must include the Malware and DLP quarantine library names.
If you are onboarding the tenant for DLP and Malware, you need to create two libraries for quarantine policy actions.
Name: Enter Zscaler_Quarantine.
Unique Name: Enter Malware_Quarantine.
set their permission to Library Administrator, and click Add.
but enter Zscaler_DLP_Quarantine for the Name and DLP_Quarantine for the Unique Name.

salesforce-user.statement: In the sandbox steps the Salesforce user is created with the Salesforce user license and a System Administrator profile, and the permission set's license is Salesforce; the production steps give the permission set's license as Salesforce API Integration and refer to the Salesforce integration user created in the previous section.

quotes: selecting Salesforce for the User License, and System Administrator for the Profile.
License: Select Salesforce.
License: Select Salesforce API Integration.
Select the Salesforce integration user you created in the previous section.

salesforce-client-app.statement: In the sandbox steps the Salesforce external client app has Distribution State Local, callback URL https://test.salesforce.com and scopes Perform Requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access) and Manage user data via APIs (api). It enables the JWT Bearer Flow and requires a secret for the Web Server Flow and the Refresh Token Flow. Its OAuth policies pre-authorize admin approved users, relax IP restrictions, keep the refresh token valid until revoked and set a session timeout of 1,440 minutes (24 hours), and its app policy profile is Minimum Access - API Only Integrations.

quotes: Select Distribution State as Local.
Enter the following for Callback URL: https://test.salesforce.com.
Perform Requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access)
Manage user data via APIs (api)
In the Flow Enablement section, select Enable JWT Bearer Flow.
In the Security section, select Require secret for Web Server Flow and Require secret for Refresh Token Flow checkboxes.
Permitted Users: Select Admin approved users are pre-authorized.
IP Relaxation: Select Relax IP restrictions.
Refresh Token Policy: Select Refresh token is valid until revoked.
Session Timeout In Minutes: Select 1,440 (24 hours).
Under App Policies, Select Profiles: Select Minimum Access - API Only Integrations.

salesforce-org-settings.statement: The sandbox steps for Salesforce uncheck the Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated checkbox and check Enable Salesforce CRM Content.

quotes: Uncheck the Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated checkbox and click Save.
Check the Enable Salesforce CRM Content checkbox and click Save.

salesforce-key.statement: The custom onboarding process for Salesforce requires uploading the private key file to the Admin Console. Zscaler recommends a certificate authority-signed (CA-signed) certificate, and a self-signed certificate can also be used if a CA-signed one cannot be obtained.

quotes: The custom onboarding process for Salesforce requires uploading your private key file to the Zscaler Admin Console.
Zscaler recommends generating a certificate authority-signed (CA-signed) certificate which can be a more authoritative way to prove that your organization’s data communications are genuine.
If you are unable to obtain the CA-signed certificate, a self-signed certificate can also be used.

salesforce-authorize.statement: Authorizing a Salesforce tenant in the Admin Console selects Custom for SaaS Connector and, in the sandbox steps, Sandbox Account for the Tenant Type. An optional section, Configure External Trusted Domains & User Profiles, allows up to 1,000 domains and up to 1,000 email addresses.

quotes: SaaS Connector: Select Custom.
Select Sandbox Account for the Tenant Type.
(Optional) Under (Optional) Configure External Trusted Domains & User Profiles:
You can add up to 1,000 domains.
You can add up to 1,000 email addresses.

salesforce-permissions.statement: The sandbox permissions table lists, for DLP and Malware onboarding, Manage Salesforce CRM Content, Query All Files, Access Libraries, View All Users, Manage Chatter Messages and Direct Messages and Manage Unlisted Groups with the action Scanning, together with View Event Log Files with Scanning and Modify All Data with Apply Policy Actions, and, for SSPM, Query All Files, View Health Check, Modify All Data, Modify Metadata Through Metadata API Functions, Manage Certificates and Manage Sharing with the action SSPM Scan.
salesforce-permissions.conditions: The captured tables are misaligned: continuation rows put the permission in the first column. The reading follows the row order under each Onboarding heading.

quotes: | App Permissions | DLP and Malware | Manage Salesforce CRM Content | Scanning
| Query All Files | Scanning
| System Permissions | DLP and Malware | Access Libraries | Scanning
| View All Users | Scanning
| View Event Log Files | Scanning
| Modify All Data | Apply Policy Actions
| Manage Chatter Messages and Direct Messages | Scanning
| Manage Unlisted Groups | Scanning
| SSPM | Query All Files | SSPM Scan
| SSPM | View Health Check | SSPM Scan
| Modify All Data | SSPM Scan
| Modify Metadata Through Metadata API Functions | SSPM Scan
| Manage Certificates | SSPM Scan
| Manage Sharing | SSPM Scan

salesforce-production-permissions.statement: The production permissions table maps View Event Log Files to Generate SaaS Activities and Modify All Data to Scanning, and has a Field Permissions row, Read Access for Description, Subject, and Type Fields, with Scanning. Its SSPM rows include Modify All Data with SSPM Scan.

quotes: | View Event Log Files | Generate SaaS Activities
| Modify All Data | Scanning
| Field Permissions | DLP and Malware | Read Access for Description, Subject, and Type Fields | Scanning
| Modify All Data | SSPM Scan

microsoft-apps-and-methods.statement: Microsoft custom connectors cover Exchange, Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) Labels, OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, Teams, Dynamics 365, Copilot and Microsoft 365. Choosing the client secret option requires the Client ID, Client Secret and Tenant ID; choosing the private key option requires the Client ID, Tenant ID and the Private Key PEM file.

quotes: The Zscaler service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to the following Microsoft applications: Exchange, Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) Labels, OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, Teams, Dynamics 365, Copilot, and Microsoft 365.
Choosing the client secret option requires you to provide your Client ID, Client Secret, and Tenant ID.
Choosing the private key option requires the Client ID, Tenant ID, and the Private Key PEM file.

microsoft-registration.statement: Zscaler recommends creating a new connector for each Microsoft application. The app registration's supported account types are set to Accounts in any organizational directory (Any Microsoft Entra ID tenant - Multitenant), with Web as the redirect platform and the Zscaler account URL (for example https://console.zscaler.com/). The client secret value is displayed only once, and specific API permissions are assigned for each connector, with Grant admin consent where required, such as SharePoint permissions.

quotes: Zscaler recommends creating a new connector for each Microsoft application to ensure isolation and better management.
Supported account types: Ensure that this option is set to the Accounts in any organizational directory (Any Microsoft Entra ID tenant - Multitenant) value.
Redirect URI (optional): Select Web as the platform, then provide the URL of the Zscaler account (e.g., https://console.zscaler.com/).
The client secret value is displayed only once and cannot be retrieved after you navigate away from the page.
You must assign specific API permissions for each Microsoft connector you create for the Zscaler service.
If admin consent is required (such as SharePoint permissions), select Grant admin consent.

microsoft-pem-files.statement: The private key method uses private_key.pem (an AES-256 encrypted RSA private key, used to create combined.pem), certificate.pem (a self-signed certificate, uploaded in the Azure portal) and combined.pem (the private key and certificate together, uploaded on the Internet & SaaS onboarding page); the password is entered when prompted.

quotes: private_key.pem | AES-256 encrypted RSA private key | Used to create combined.pem.
certificate.pem | Self-signed certificate | Upload in Azure portal.
combined.pem | Combined PEM file containing the private key and certificate | Upload on Internet & SaaS onboarding page.
evidence.after: This section covers how to generate your private key PEM file

quotes: Enter your password when prompted.

microsoft-consent-url.statement: To authorize a custom connector, the Azure login URL is first updated manually to grant permissions on the tenant: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/adminconsent for Microsoft 365 and Microsoft 365 GCC tenants and https://login.microsoftonline.us/common/adminconsent for Microsoft 365 GCC High and Microsoft 365 DoD tenants, each with the client_id, a state of administration/add-casb-tenants and the redirect_uri; MIP uses a state of administration/mip-labels.

quotes: To authorize a custom connector, you must first manually update the Azure login URL to grant permissions for the application on the tenant.
For Microsoft 365 and Microsoft 365 GCC tenants: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/adminconsent?client_id=<client_id>&state=administration/add-casb-tenants&redirect_uri=<redirect_uri>
For Microsoft 365 GCC High and Microsoft 365 DoD tenants: https://login.microsoftonline.us/common/adminconsent?client_id=<client_id>&state=administration/add-casb-tenants&redirect_uri=<redirect_uri>
https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/adminconsent?client_id=<client_id>&state=administration/mip-labels&redirect_uri=<redirect_uri>

microsoft-app-specifics.statement: For Microsoft Azure Blob Storage the application needs extra role assignments in Azure, Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Account Contributor. Copilot registration is completed by running a script through the Power Platform API or PowerShell for Power Platform administrators. An MIP account displays Validation Successful if authorized and, on Validation Failed, can be reauthorized with Reauthorize on the Edit MIP Account window.

quotes: If you are setting up a custom connector for Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, you must add additional role assignments in Azure to ensure that the Zscaler service can properly access the application.
Select Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Account Contributor and then click Next.
To complete the app registration for Copilot, run the following script in Azure via Power Platform API or PowerShell for Power Platform administrators.
The MIP Account displays a status of Validation Successful if the account is authorized.
If the status on the MIP account is Validation Failed, you can try the authorization process again by clicking Reauthorize on the Edit MIP Account window.

google-service-account.statement: The Google connector steps create a service account key of type JSON, and the private key JSON file downloaded while creating the service account is uploaded with Authorize. Domain wide delegation is managed with MANAGE DOMAIN WIDE DELEGATION, the Gmail service account is given the Pub/Sub Admin role, and a value entered at onboarding is treated as the tenant ID, from which Zscaler internally fetches the tenant domain.

quotes: In the Grant this service account access to project section, select the role Pub/Sub Admin and click Continue.
select the key type as JSON and click Create.
Click MANAGE DOMAIN WIDE DELEGATION.
This value is treated as the tenant ID, and Zscaler internally fetches the tenant domain from it.
Upload the private key JSON file that you downloaded while creating a service account and click Authorize.
evidence.after: Log in to the Google Cloud Platform and select any project or create a new project within the organization.

gcp-roles.statement: For a Google Cloud Platform connector the admin is told to use the role name exactly as provided and not to modify or rename the role. With one of the permission types the page describes, Report Incident and Action None policy actions function and Sign-in Events, Webhooks and other policy actions do not; another configuration gives the connector sufficient permission to register webhooks while keeping the read role intact on Google Cloud Storage, and Sign-in Events do not function with a further set of permissions. If Zscaler_Read_role is modified, a scan restart is mandatory for the changes to take effect.

quotes: With these permissions, Report Incident and Action None policy actions will function. Sign-in Events, Webhooks, and other policy actions will not function.
This configuration provides connector sufficient permission to register webhooks along with keeping read role intact on Google Cloud Storage.
Sign-in Events will not function with these permissions.
If you do modify the Zscaler_Read_role, a scan restart is mandatory for the changes to take effect.
Use the role name exactly as provided and do not modify or rename the role.
evidence.after: Start by setting up one of the following permission types:

gcp-setup.statement: For a GCP storage scan the service account is created without granting access or permissions to the project and added as an IAM member of the organization with Zscaler_Read_Role or Zscaler_ReadWrite_Role. Audit logs are enabled for Google Cloud Storage and the Cloud Logging API with Data Write, Data Read and Admin Read. At onboarding the Connector Role is Read or Read Write, and with Read Write the Quarantine Bucket name is also entered.

quotes: Click Continue without granting access or permissions to the project.
This service account must be added as an IAM member in the organization you are setting up for storage scan.
Click Select a role and select Zscaler_Read_Role or Zscaler_ReadWrite_Role.
On the Audit Logs page, search for Google Cloud Storage and Cloud Logging API and select both services.
select Data Write, Data Read, and Admin Read in the Log Type tab and click Save.
Select either Read or Read Write for the Connector Role.
Enter the Organization ID and if you selected Read Write as the connector role, also enter the Quarantine Bucket name.

salesforce-modify-all-data.summary: The Salesforce custom connector page lists Modify All Data under SSPM onboarding with the action SSPM Scan, while the SSPM permissions page marks it required only for remediation.

quotes: | Modify All Data | SSPM Scan

positions.says: Modify All Data is listed with the action SSPM Scan.

quotes: | Permission Sets > System Permissions: Modify All Data | User with License: Salesforce/Salesforce API Integration Profile: System Administrator/Minimum Access - API Only Integrations | No | No | No | Yes | To perform remediation

positions.says: Modify All Data is marked No in three columns and Yes in one, with the purpose To perform remediation.

salesforce-modify-all-data.impact: Whether a Salesforce SSPM scan needs Modify All Data, or only remediation does, depends on which page governs; the pages do not say. The connector page also lists Modify All Data for DLP and Malware, with Apply Policy Actions in the sandbox table and Scanning in the production table. The graph's claim in zia.sspm.permissions:salesforce-inevitable-write follows the SSPM page.

trusted-profiles-scope.summary: The tenants page says external trusted domains and users apply only to email SaaS application tenants, while the Salesforce (CRM) custom connector authorization offers External Trusted Domains and User Profiles.

quotes: Displays the total number of added external trusted domains. Click to view a list of the domains. This only applies to email SaaS application tenants.

positions.says: The trusted domains count applies only to email SaaS application tenants.

quotes: (Optional) Under (Optional) Configure External Trusted Domains & User Profiles:
You can add up to 1,000 domains.

positions.says: The Salesforce authorization step offers an optional trusted domains and user profiles section with up to 1,000 domains.

trusted-profiles-scope.impact: Whether trusted domains and users apply to a Salesforce tenant is stated both ways; the graph's claim zia.casb.tenants:trusted-profiles-email-only follows the tenants page. The relation of the 1,000-entry figure to the 32-profile limit is not stated.

microsoft-mip-client-secret.summary: The Microsoft connector page says MIP requires the private key method and the client secret method is not available, while its own table marks MIP Yes in both method columns and its MIP account steps enter a Client Secret.

quotes: Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MIP), SharePoint, Copilot, and Microsoft 365 require the private key method for onboarding; the client secret method is not available.

positions.says: MIP, SharePoint, Copilot and Microsoft 365 require the private key method; the client secret method is not available.

quotes: MIP | Yes | Yes
Enter the values for the Client ID, Client Secret, and Tenant ID that you copied earlier, then click Validate.

positions.says: The table row for MIP reads Yes | Yes, and a step enters Client ID, Client Secret and Tenant ID.

microsoft-mip-client-secret.impact: Whether an MIP connector can be onboarded with a client secret is stated both ways on one page; the page does not say which governs.

salesforce-production-values.title: Production Salesforce values on the connector page
salesforce-production-values.detail: Diffing the two sections shows the Production Tenant steps repeat the sandbox callback URL https://test.salesforce.com and Select Sandbox Account for the Tenant Type, and omit the Enable Salesforce CRM Content step. The production permissions differ from the sandbox ones (salesforce-production-permissions). The page gives no production callback URL or tenant type and does not say production does not need the CRM Content step.

dynamics-permissions.title: Dynamics 365 permissions
dynamics-permissions.detail: Dynamics 365 is in the Microsoft method table but the page has no permissions table for it.
